description: Explainable, evidence-backed industry-to-technology recommendation layer for the Industrial Energy Transition Optimizer.
purpose: Provides industry-specific technology classifications, reasons, source traceability, operational considerations and cluster recommendations. Hard engineering feasibility remains in technology_rules.json.

source_context.source: NITI Aayog Roadmap for Green Transition of MSMEs
source_context.relevance: Indian MSME textile energy and decarbonisation context
Industrial heat electrification and technology suitability

source_context.source: Decarbonizing MSMEs: Use of Biomass for Green Steam and Heat Applications
source_context.relevance: Biomass-based steam and heat pathways for textile MSMEs

heat_pump.reason: Suitable for low-temperature textile wet-processing, hot-water and drying-related heat where the required process temperature is within the technology's operating range.
cluster_recommendations: Prioritize textile wet-processing clusters with significant low-temperature steam or hot-water demand.
Consider pairing with thermal storage where process demand is variable.
Use renewable electricity where available to improve emissions performance.

electric_boiler.reason: Suitable for textile steam and hot-water applications where electrical capacity and process temperature requirements are compatible.
cluster_recommendations: Prioritize textile dyeing and wet-processing clusters with existing steam systems.
Assess demand charges and available sanctioned electrical capacity before selection.
Consider coupling with solar PV and thermal storage.

biomass_boiler.reason: Biomass-based steam and heat are explicitly identified as a practical decarbonisation pathway for textile MSMEs, with potential to replace fossil-fuel heat where biomass supply is reliable.
biomass_boiler.source: Decarbonizing MSMEs: Use of Biomass for Green Steam and Heat Applications (MNRE/GIZ/Grant Thornton)
cluster_recommendations: Prioritize textile clusters located near reliable agricultural-residue supply chains.
Consider multi-fuel boiler configurations to reduce seasonal supply risk.
Evaluate pellet/briquette logistics and delivered cost rather than only biomass commodity price.

solar_thermal.reason: Can provide useful low-to-moderate temperature heat for suitable textile processes, but performance depends on solar resource, available area and process load matching.
solar_thermal.source: Electrifying Industrial Heat in India (2026) / MNRE-GIZ biomass and green-heat context
cluster_recommendations: Prioritize sites with strong solar availability and sufficient roof or land area.
Use as a hybrid source with electric or biomass systems where continuous heat is required.

solar_pv.reason: Solar PV is not a direct process-heat technology but can materially improve the economics and emissions profile of electrified textile heat systems.
cluster_recommendations: Use as an enabling technology for heat pumps and electric boilers.
Consider captive or group-captive renewable procurement where individual MSME scale is insufficient.

thermal_storage.reason: Useful for decoupling heat production from heat demand and improving the integration of intermittent renewable heat and electricity.
thermal_storage.source: Electrifying Industrial Heat in India (2026) / FlexiHeat-DST (2026)
cluster_recommendations: Consider where textile production has variable or shift-based thermal demand.

waste_heat_recovery.reason: Useful for recovering heat from dryers, thermic-fluid systems and other textile processes before replacing the remaining fossil heat demand.
waste_heat_recovery.source: NITI Aayog Roadmap for Green Transition of MSMEs (2026) and textile efficiency evidence in project knowledge base
cluster_recommendations: Evaluate waste heat before sizing replacement heating equipment.

source_context.source: Decarbonizing MSMEs: Use of Biomass for Green Steam and Heat Applications
source_context.relevance: Biomass green steam and heat in food-processing MSMEs
Industrial electrification for low- and moderate-temperature heat

heat_pump.reason: Food-processing operations commonly include hot-water, drying, washing and other low-to-moderate temperature loads suitable for heat-pump integration.
cluster_recommendations: Prioritize low-temperature washing, drying and hot-water applications.
Use waste heat as a potential heat source where available.

electric_boiler.reason: Suitable for food-processing steam and hot-water demand when electricity infrastructure is adequate.
cluster_recommendations: Prioritize plants with stable electrical infrastructure and manageable demand charges.

biomass_boiler.reason: Biomass can provide green steam and process heat for food-processing MSMEs, particularly where agricultural residues are locally accessible.
biomass_boiler.source: Decarbonizing MSMEs: Use of Biomass for Green Steam and Heat Applications (MNRE/GIZ/Grant Thornton)
cluster_recommendations: Prioritize agricultural-processing clusters with nearby biomass residues.
Assess delivered biomass cost and supply reliability.

solar_thermal.reason: Useful for low-temperature process heat and hot-water loads where solar availability and space are adequate.
cluster_recommendations: Use for daytime hot-water and compatible thermal loads.

solar_pv.reason: Can reduce the electricity cost and emissions intensity of electrified food-processing heat systems.
cluster_recommendations: Pair with heat pumps or electric boilers where feasible.

thermal_storage.reason: Can shift heat production and help integrate intermittent renewable electricity or solar heat.
cluster_recommendations: Prioritize facilities with batch-based thermal demand.

waste_heat_recovery.reason: Waste heat can reduce the amount of new heat supply required in food-processing facilities.
waste_heat_recovery.source: Roadmap for Green Transition of MSMEs (2026)
cluster_recommendations: Evaluate heat recovery before replacing boilers or heaters.

source_context.relevance: Wide range of industrial temperature requirements and electrification economics

source_context.source: Decarbonizing MSMEs: Use of Biomass for Green Steam and Heat Applications
source_context.relevance: Biomass heat and steam for chemical MSMEs

heat_pump.reason: Applicable to low- and moderate-temperature chemical heating where process temperature and materials compatibility permit.
cluster_recommendations: Prioritize low-temperature utility and recovery applications rather than assuming suitability for all chemical processes.

electric_boiler.reason: Can provide steam and hot water for chemical processing where grid capacity and pressure requirements are compatible.
cluster_recommendations: Prioritize utility steam systems with predictable load profiles.

biomass_boiler.reason: Biomass-based steam and heat are applicable in chemical MSMEs but require reliable fuel quality, handling and emissions-management arrangements.
biomass_boiler.source: Decarbonizing MSMEs: Use of Biomass for Green Steam and Heat Applications (MNRE/GIZ/Grant Thornton)
cluster_recommendations: Use primarily where a reliable industrial biomass supply chain exists.

solar_pv.reason: Can provide low-carbon electricity for electrified utilities and auxiliary loads.
cluster_recommendations: Consider captive or group-captive renewable electricity for cluster-level cost reduction.

thermal_storage.reason: Can support load shifting and renewable integration where thermal demand can be decoupled from production.
cluster_recommendations: Use where batch operations permit thermal buffering.

waste_heat_recovery.reason: Chemical plants can have valuable waste-heat streams; recovering them can reduce replacement heat demand.
waste_heat_recovery.source: Roadmap for Green Transition of MSMEs (2026)
cluster_recommendations: Screen waste-heat opportunities before selecting new primary heating equipment.

source_context.source: Decarbonizing MSMEs: Use of Biomass for Green Steam and Heat Applications
source_context.relevance: Biomass-based steam and heat in pharmaceutical MSMEs
Electrification technologies for lower-temperature industrial heat

heat_pump.reason: Suitable for lower-temperature hot-water, drying and utility heat where hygienic and process specifications permit.
cluster_recommendations: Prioritize low-temperature utility and process heat first.

electric_boiler.reason: Provides controllable steam and hot water for pharmaceutical processes where adequate electric capacity exists.
cluster_recommendations: Assess electrical reliability and backup requirements before full conversion.

biomass_boiler.reason: Biomass can provide steam and heat, but pharmaceutical sites require careful fuel handling, emissions control and compliance with process/environmental requirements.
biomass_boiler.source: Decarbonizing MSMEs: Use of Biomass for Green Steam and Heat Applications (MNRE/GIZ/Grant Thornton)
cluster_recommendations: Prefer applications where boiler-room separation and emissions-control infrastructure are practical.

solar_thermal.reason: Can serve compatible hot-water and low-temperature thermal loads when solar resource and space allow.
cluster_recommendations: Use as a supplemental rather than sole source for reliability-critical processes.

solar_pv.reason: Can lower the carbon intensity and operating cost of electrically supplied utilities.
cluster_recommendations: Pair with electric boilers and heat pumps where appropriate.

waste_heat_recovery.reason: Waste heat recovery can reduce utility energy demand before primary heating conversion.
waste_heat_recovery.source: Roadmap for Green Transition of MSMEs (2026)
cluster_recommendations: Prioritize clean, recoverable heat streams.

source_context.source: Decarbonizing MSMEs: Use of Biomass for Green Steam and Heat Applications
source_context.relevance: Biomass steam and heat opportunities in paper MSMEs

heat_pump.reason: Applicable primarily to low-temperature utility or drying-related heat where temperature requirements are within the technology's range.
cluster_recommendations: Prioritize low-temperature recovery and utility applications.

electric_boiler.reason: Can replace fossil steam production where electricity supply and process economics are acceptable.
cluster_recommendations: Evaluate grid and tariff constraints carefully.

biomass_boiler.reason: Paper manufacturing can benefit from biomass-based heat and steam, particularly where compatible residues are available.
biomass_boiler.source: Decarbonizing MSMEs: Use of Biomass for Green Steam and Heat Applications (MNRE/GIZ/Grant Thornton)
cluster_recommendations: Prioritize paper clusters with strong local biomass or process-residue supply.

solar_thermal.reason: Potentially useful for compatible low-temperature heat loads but not a universal replacement for high-temperature paper-process demand.
cluster_recommendations: Use for compatible auxiliary heat rather than assuming full-process coverage.

solar_pv.reason: Can reduce electricity expenditure and emissions for electrified equipment and auxiliaries.
cluster_recommendations: Consider captive or group-captive renewable procurement.

thermal_storage.reason: Can buffer compatible thermal loads and support integration of variable renewable sources.
cluster_recommendations: Use for demand profiles compatible with thermal buffering.

waste_heat_recovery.reason: Waste heat recovery is particularly relevant in energy-intensive thermal operations and can reduce the required replacement heat supply.
waste_heat_recovery.source: Roadmap for Green Transition of MSMEs (2026)
cluster_recommendations: Assess recovery from exhaust and process streams before primary-fuel switching.

source_context.relevance: Induction, resistance, arc and plasma technology selection

source_context.source: CEEW Notes: Advancing India's Green Steel Transition
source_context.relevance: MSME steel/DRI cluster decarbonisation and readiness/cost perspective

heat_pump.reason: Primary steel and foundry melting processes generally require temperatures well above the practical range of industrial heat pumps.
heat_pump.source: Electrifying Industrial Heat in India (2026) / FlexiHeat-DST (2026)
cluster_recommendations: Do not select for primary metal melting.
Consider only for auxiliary low-temperature heat where separately justified.

electric_boiler.reason: Can serve steam or hot-water utility loads but is not a substitute for high-temperature steel melting equipment.
cluster_recommendations: Use for utility heat rather than core melting.

biomass_boiler.reason: Can serve compatible auxiliary steam or thermal requirements, but biomass combustion is not treated as a universal substitute for electric high-temperature furnaces.
biomass_boiler.source: Decarbonizing MSMEs: Use of Biomass for Green Steam and Heat Applications (MNRE/GIZ/Grant Thornton)
cluster_recommendations: Restrict to compatible auxiliary heat applications.

induction_furnace.reason: Induction furnaces are well suited to high-temperature metal melting and heating, with direct electromagnetic heating, precise control and strong applicability in foundry and metal-processing operations.
cluster_recommendations: Prioritize foundry and metal-processing clusters with adequate electrical infrastructure.
Evaluate power quality and demand charges, not only energy tariffs.

resistance_furnace.reason: Resistance heating is suitable for controlled high-temperature heating and specialised furnace applications, particularly where uniform temperature is required.
cluster_recommendations: Prioritize applications requiring controlled and uniform heating rather than high-throughput scrap melting.

electric_arc_furnace.reason: Electric arc furnaces are established for high-temperature steelmaking and scrap-based melting and can materially reduce direct fossil-fuel use.
electric_arc_furnace.source: FlexiHeat-DST (2026) / Electrifiying Industrial Heat in India (2026)
cluster_recommendations: Prioritize clusters with strong grid infrastructure and scrap availability.

plasma_technology.reason: Plasma technology can provide extremely high-temperature concentrated heat but is more specialised and should be evaluated for applications where its thermal characteristics justify the complexity.
cluster_recommendations: Consider for specialised high-temperature operations rather than as a default MSME option.

solar_pv.reason: Solar electricity can lower the electricity cost and emissions of electrified furnace technologies, although storage, grid and power-quality requirements remain important.
cluster_recommendations: Explore group-captive or cluster-level renewable electricity procurement.

waste_heat_recovery.reason: Waste heat recovery can reduce thermal losses and offset auxiliary energy requirements, especially in energy-intensive metal-processing facilities.
waste_heat_recovery.source: CEEW 2026 steel-cluster research / Roadmap for Green Transition of MSMEs
cluster_recommendations: Screen waste-heat opportunities before adding new primary energy supply.
